basis: Intellectual disability and craniofacial skeletal malformations principally define the syndrome. Cardiac defects and hearing loss lack established frequencies of at least 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: principal craniofacial skeletal malformations, including brachy/plagiocephaly and micrognathia, are explicitly defining features.

basis: The susceptibility syndrome is defined by its CNS glioma target; this organ assignment does not establish an existing tumour.

decisions.neurologic: primary: CNS glioma defines this organ-specific susceptibility syndrome; no_axis is reserved for concepts whose organs fall outside the axes.

basis: Hypomyelinating CNS disease; pes cavus in 3/3 and sensorineural hearing loss in 30-79%. Gaze and sphincter findings do not establish direct ocular or urinary-tract damage.

decisions.renal: none: sphincter dysfunction occurs in 30-79%, but reflects neurologic dysfunction without established direct urinary-tract damage.
decisions.ocular: none: strabismus and slow saccades accompany CNS dysfunction; intrinsic eye damage or loss of vision is not established.

basis: Respiratory-chain metabolic disorder; brain atrophy and seizures in 3/3. Blindness in 1/1 assessed and strabismus in 2/3 support ocular involvement, with limited sampling.

decisions.neurologic: involved: brain atrophy and seizures occur in 3/3; the concept is defined by respiratory-chain deficiency rather than a specific neurologic syndrome.

basis: Inherited skeletal-muscle channelopathies with potassium-related paralytic attacks. Neuropathy and cardiac involvement are subtype-specific.

decisions.neurologic: none: the usual disease process impairs skeletal-muscle excitability; its neurologic classification does not establish direct CNS or peripheral-nerve damage.

basis: Congenital myopathy and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; persistent ptosis affects eyelid function in 4/5. A single assessed septal defect does not establish common cardiac involvement.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent ptosis in 4/5 represents impaired eyelid elevation from the congenital myopathy; eyelids are explicitly within the ocular axis.

basis: Hydrocephalus and severe neurologic dysfunction define HSAS; characteristic adducted thumbs and structural thumb contractures are defining features, reported in 20/20.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: adducted thumbs are explicitly part of the disease definition, with structural thumb contractures documented in 20/20.

basis: FIG4-associated ALS is a motor-neuron disease; muscle wasting and bulbar weakness result from denervation rather than direct muscle pathology.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy is common over the ALS course but results from motor-neuron denervation, without a direct skeletal-muscle disease process.

basis: Both spinal-cord splitting and an incomplete osseous spur are defining congenital malformations of this subtype.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the incomplete bony spur is a defining skeletal malformation intrinsic to this subtype; a separate skeletal diagnosis is unnecessary.

basis: Metabolic enzyme deficiency; muscle injury supported by elevated CK in 80-99% and myoglobinuria in 30-79%; palmoplantar hyperkeratosis 30-79%. Renal insufficiency occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: elevated CK in 80-99% and myoglobinuria in 30-79% establish common muscle injury; the umbrella concept is defined by the metabolic enzyme defect.
